correctness.rationale: The modular model was independently checked for symmetry, no loops, degree seven, and 0 or 1 common neighbor for adjacent or distinct nonadjacent pairs, respectively, identifying the specified strongly regular graph. Initial observation is N[S] at t=1. During a wave an observed vertex contributes its sole unobserved neighbor if there is exactly one; the mask is updated only after scanning all contributing vertices. No-change states fail; every changing step strictly shrinks the missing set, so the process terminates. An independent batched recount exhausts all sets of sizes 1 through 6 (empty trivially fails), split by the smallest selected label into [0,2), [2,6), and [6,50). It visits 50, 1225, 19600, 230300, 2118760, and 15890700 sets respectively, with no successes below size six. For six, the only nonzero (round, induced edges):count cells are (2,0):12950, (3,0):448000, (3,1):63000, (4,0):378000, (4,1):630000, (4,2):294000, (5,1):378000, (5,2):126000. Their sum is 2329950, with the given probability 317/2162. Round one cannot observe all fifty because at most 48 neighborhood incidences are available. The two bundled C++ programs were inspected: they implement the stated graph constructions, compositional iteration, synchronous forcing and edge count under the same convention. The proof only concerns this graph.
residual_risks: Bundled code was not run and no saved bundled run output was present; the independent recount covers the whole finite claim rather than relying on that output. The round index shifts by one under conventions that omit the initial observation.

value.rationale: The Hoffman–Singleton graph is a canonical highly symmetric test case. The joint distribution answers a natural question left open by sensor minimization: how time-to-observe and the adjacency pattern of minimum sensor sets vary together. The exact cells give sharp time extremes, the exclusion of three induced edges, and an optimum-set density; none is mechanically fixed by the strongly regular parameters or by the optimum size alone. These data can serve as a benchmark for graph-specific structural or computational accounts of power domination.
residual_risks: A finite benchmark, not a structural description of every optimum or a law for other graphs.
